mainTopic: Mistaken and forced חליצה and גט, and identifying the parties for חליצה and מיאון
overview: A ברייתא teaches that a 'mistaken' חליצה is valid, and the גמרא asks what that means. ריש לקיש says it is when the יבם is told that doing חליצה will marry him to her. רבי יוחנן rejects this, because חליצה needs both sides to intend it. He explains instead that it is a חליצה done in return for a promise of two hundred זוז, and a ברייתא with a story about רבי חייא supports him. Two stories follow. In the first, רבי חייא בר אבא tricks a יבם and then has him do a proper חליצה. In the second, רב פפא corrects אביי to use the two-hundred-זוז method, and he proves from the case of an escaping prisoner that the woman need not pay, since she can say 'I was fooling you.' Next, a ברייתא compares mistaken and forced חליצה and גט. The גמרא explains that a forced act is valid only if the man ends up saying 'רוצה אני,' and brings a proof from forcing someone to bring a קרבן. Finally, רב הונא and רבא disagree about whether a court must recognize the people before doing חליצה or מיאון, and how that affects writing documents about it.

steps.title: A mistaken חליצה is valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a 'mistaken' חליצה is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A mistaken חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says a חליצה done under some kind of mistake still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the rule but never says what 'mistaken' means. That missing definition is what the rest of the sugya will try to fill in.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony of removing the shoe, which frees a widow from the יבם

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A mistaken ḥalitza is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חליצה done under a mistake is still valid.

steps.title: What counts as a mistaken חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definition of a 'mistaken' חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a mistaken חליצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of case the ברייתא means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Mistaken' could mean many things, and some mistakes would surely ruin the חליצה. The גמרא needs to know exactly which mistake still lets it work.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one is it? What case is meant?

phrases.english: What is a mistaken ḥalitza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of mistake is meant by 'mistaken חליצה'.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: he was told חליצה would marry her
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says it is a case where the יבם was told that doing חליצה is how he marries her.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Any case where they tell him, 'Do חליצה, and with this you are marrying her.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers: the mistake is that the יבם thought the חליצה was a way to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, even though the man wanted to marry her, the act of חליצה still counts. So she is now free to marry others.

keyTerms.meaning: Do חליצה (let her remove your shoe)
You marry her (take her in as a wife)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Any case where they say to him: Do ḥalitza,
and by this you are marrying her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A mistaken חליצה is one where the יבם was told the חליצה would marry her to him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both sides must have the right intent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן cites a teaching that חליצה is invalid unless both the man and the woman intend it, so ריש לקיש's case can't be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: I learned that if he intended and she didn't, or she intended and he didn't, the חליצה is invalid until both intend together. And you say the חליצה is valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's explanation. He quotes a teaching that a חליצה needs both people to have the right intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ריש לקיש's case the man did not intend real חליצה at all. He thought he was marrying her. Since a חליצה without both people's intent is invalid, ריש לקיש's case cannot be the 'valid mistaken חליצה'.

keyTerms.meaning: I learn / I have a teaching that says

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying a mistaken חליצה is invalid. He agrees with the ברייתא. He only rejects ריש לקיש's example of what the mistake is.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: I teach:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּון הוּא וְלֹא נִתְכַּוְּונָה הִיא,
phrases.english: whether he intended and she did not intend,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנִּתְכַּוְּונָה הִיא וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון הוּא —
phrases.english: or she intended and he did not intend —
her ḥalitza is invalid,
until both of them intend together.
And you say her ḥalitza is valid?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's definition of a mistaken חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חליצה requires both parties to intend it. In ריש לקיש's case the man intended marriage, not חליצה, so the חליצה should be invalid, not valid.

steps.title: New definition: חליצה in exchange for two hundred זוז
steps.stepSummary: Instead, a mistaken חליצה is one where the יבם is told to do חליצה on condition that she pays him two hundred זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, any case where they tell him: 'Do חליצה for her on condition that she gives you two hundred זוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן continues and replaces ריש לקיש's case with a new one: the man is persuaded to do חליצה by a promise of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the man truly intends a real חליצה, so both sides have the right intent. The 'mistake' is only about the money promise, and it does not undo the חליצה.

phrases.english: Rather, any case where they say to him:
"Do ḥalitza for her on condition
that she gives you two hundred zuz."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces ריש לקיש's rejected definition with a new one that fits רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mistake was that the man thought חליצה would marry him to her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mistake is about a money promise; the man truly intended חליצה, so it is valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the two hundred זוז case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explicitly defines a mistaken חליצה as one done on condition of receiving two hundred זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: A mistaken חליצה is valid. What is a mistaken חליצה? Any case where they say: 'Do חליצה for her on condition that she gives you two hundred זוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what the new definition said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the answer of step 5 with an earlier source. It shows the two hundred זוז case is not just a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught so in a ברייתא (a supporting source)

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
A mistaken ḥalitza is valid.
What is a mistaken ḥalitza —
any case where they say:
Do ḥalitza for her on condition
that she gives you two hundred zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition given in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The definition of a mistaken חליצה as one done for a promise of two hundred זוז.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states this definition word for word.

steps.title: The story before רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells of a woman whose unsuitable יבם was told to do חליצה for two hundred זוז, and רבי חייא ruled the חליצה valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about a woman who fell to a יבם who was not suitable for her. They told him: 'Do חליצה for her on condition that she gives you two hundred זוז.' The case came before רבי חייא, and he ruled it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a real case that shows this rule being used in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges used the money promise to get the unsuitable יבם to agree to חליצה. רבי חייא ruled that the חליצה stands, which shows the two hundred זוז case is the valid 'mistaken חליצה'.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, a real case that happened
The brother of the dead husband

steps.whatToRemember: A 'mistaken חליצה' that is valid is NOT where the man thought he was marrying her, since both sides must intend real חליצה. It is where he did real חליצה because he was promised two hundred זוז.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a בית דין may use a money promise to get an unsuitable יבם to do חליצה, and the חליצה still works.

phrases.english: And there was a story with a certain woman
who fell before a yavam
phrases.notes: 'Fell before' means she became bound to him for יבום after her husband died.

phrases.english: who was not suitable for her,
and they said to him:
"Do ḥalitza for her on condition
that she gives you two hundred zuz,"
and the case came before Rabbi Ḥiyya
and he ruled it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of step 6 with a story that confirms the rule.
steps.raayaObject: That a חליצה done for a promise of two hundred זוז is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case ruled on by רבי חייא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חליצה done for a promise of money is the valid 'mistaken חליצה'.

steps.title: A woman refuses her יבם before רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: A יבם brings his יבמה before רבי חייא בר אבא hoping to marry her. She makes it clear that she refuses, because he only wants her money.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came before רבי חייא בר אבא. רבי חייא told the woman, 'My daughter, stand up!' She answered, 'Say that her sitting is her standing.' He asked, 'Do you know him?' She said, 'Yes. He has seen money in her, and he wants to eat it up from her.' He asked, 'Is he not pleasing to you?' She said, 'No.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a real-life story that sets up the next move. A woman tells רבי חייא בר אבא that she does not want יבום with this יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This conversation establishes the facts: the יבם wants to marry her, and she firmly refuses because he is after her money. That is exactly the kind of unsuitable יבם the earlier steps were discussing. The story is about to show how a judge handles him in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not pleasing to you?

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba.
He said to her: My daughter, stand up!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: אֵימָא יְשִׁיבָתָהּ זוֹ הִיא עֲמִידָתָהּ.
phrases.english: She said to him: Say that her sitting is her standing.
phrases.notes: She talks about herself as "her." Staying seated is her way of saying she won't even consider יבום.

phrases.english: He said to her: Do you know him?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: אִין, מָמוֹנָא הוּא דַּחֲזָא לַהּ
phrases.english: She said to him: Yes, it is money that he saw in her
and he wants to eat it up from her.
He said to her: Is he not pleasing to you?
She said to him: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא's story in step 7, the גמרא brings another practical case of an unsuitable יבם.
steps.raayaObject: How a court deals with a יבם who is unsuitable but insists on יבום
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רבי חייא בר אבא

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא tricks the יבם, then requires a proper חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא tells the יבם that doing חליצה is how he marries her. Afterward he points out that she is now forbidden to the יבם anyway, so he should do a real חליצה to free her to marry others.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to the יבם, 'Do חליצה with her, and with this you marry her.' After the יבם did חליצה, רבי חייא said, 'Now she is already forbidden to you. Do a proper חליצה with her so that she will be permitted to everyone else.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא uses ריש לקיש's trick from step 3 to get the יבם to do חליצה. He then has him do a second, fully proper חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a mistaken חליצה makes her forbidden to this יבם, so he now has nothing to lose by doing a real one. The second חליצה is done with full intent from both sides. That satisfies רבי יוחנן's rule from step 4, so she is free according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: To the world, meaning to any other man

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a practical way to satisfy both ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן: the trick gets the first חליצה done, and the second, proper חליצה removes any doubt.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do ḥalitza with her,
phrases.notes: Now רבי חייא is talking to the יבם ("him"), not to the woman.

phrases.english: and with this you marry her.
After he did ḥalitza with her, he said to him:
Now, she is already forbidden to you,
so do a proper ḥalitza with her,
so that she will be permitted to everyone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲלוֹץ לָהּ, וּבְכָךְ אַתָּה כּוֹנְסָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 8 by showing how רבי חייא freed the woman.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש's trick can be used, and then a proper חליצה should follow
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר אבא's ruling in practice

steps.title: אביי uses the same trick for רב פפא's sister-in-law
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's sister-in-law was left with a יבם unsuitable for her. אביי told the יבם that doing חליצה is how he marries her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter of רב פפא's father-in-law fell to a יבם who was not suitable for her. The case came before אביי, who said to the יבם, 'Do חליצה with her, and with this you marry her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story. אביי uses ריש לקיש's trick on an unsuitable יבם, which sets up רב פפא's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's words are exactly ריש לקיש's case from step 3. Since רבי יוחנן rejected that kind of חליצה in step 4, the ruling is open to challenge, and רב פפא will raise it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of his father-in-law, meaning his wife's sister
She fell to a יבם, meaning she now needed יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: The daughter of Rav Pappa's father-in-law

phrases.aramaic: נָפְלָה לִפְנֵי יָבָם שֶׁאֵין הָגוּן לָהּ.
phrases.english: fell before a yavam who was not suitable for her.
The case came before Abaye.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲלוֹץ לָהּ, וּבְכָךְ אַתָּה כּוֹנְסָהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Do ḥalitza with her, and with this you marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת חֲמוּהּ, דְּרַב פָּפָּא נָפְלָה לִפְנֵי יָבָם שֶׁאֵין הָגוּן לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story with the same problem, handled at first with the same trick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי tells the יבם that doing חליצה is how he marries her.

steps.title: רב פפא reminds אביי of רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: doesn't he accept רבי יוחנן's teaching that this kind of חליצה is invalid?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי, 'Doesn't the master hold of what רבי יוחנן said?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא objects to אביי's method. He points out that according to רבי יוחנן, a חליצה the יבם thinks is a marriage does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the objection from step 4: both the man and the woman must intend חליצה. A יבם who thinks he is marrying her does not intend חליצה, so the woman would still not be free.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master hold of it?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to him:
Does the master not hold
of this that Rabbi Yoḥanan said?
phrases.notes: He means the teaching from step 4: חליצה only works if both the man and the woman intend it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's ruling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's use of the 'this is how you marry her' trick
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יוחנן, a חליצה without the יבם's intent is invalid, so the trick would leave her still bound to him.

steps.title: אביי asks what else he should say
steps.stepSummary: אביי accepts the point and asks רב פפא what he should tell the יבם instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked, 'Then what should I say to him?'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not argue. He asks for a better way to get the יבם to do חליצה, which sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is still to free the woman from an unsuitable יבם. The question is how to do that in a way that also works according to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: But then, what should I say to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב פפא's challenge by asking for an alternative.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A valid way to persuade the יבם to do חליצה

steps.title: רב פפא suggests the two-hundred-זוז method
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא tells אביי to have the יבם do חליצה on condition that she pays him two hundred זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, 'Tell him: Do חליצה with her on condition that she gives you two hundred זוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the method from step 5, which רבי יוחנן accepts as a mistaken חליצה that still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the יבם knows he is doing חליצה. He is only persuaded by the promise of money. Since both sides intend חליצה, it is valid even according to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hundred זוז, a sum of money

phrases.english: He said to him: Tell him, Do ḥalitza with her

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתֵּן לְךָ מָאתַיִם זוּז.
phrases.english: on condition that she gives you two hundred zuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲלוֹץ לָהּ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתֵּן לְךָ מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Have the יבם do חליצה on condition that he is paid two hundred זוז.

steps.title: אביי tells the woman to pay
steps.stepSummary: After the חליצה, אביי tells the woman to go pay the יבם the two hundred זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the יבם did חליצה, אביי told her, 'Go give him the money.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי assumes the woman must keep her promise and pay. This sets up רב פפא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats the promise of two hundred זוז as a real debt she now owes. Whether she truly has to pay is the next question.

phrases.english: After he did ḥalitza with her,
he said to her: Go give him the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר דַּחֲלַץ לַהּ, אֲמַר לַהּ: זִיל הַב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רב פפא's method was used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי assumes she must pay the promised two hundred זוז.

steps.title: רב פפא: she was only fooling him
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the woman was only fooling the יבם, so she does not have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי, 'She did to him an "I am fooling you."'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects אביי's instruction to pay. He explains that the woman never seriously meant to pay the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise was a way to get the יבם to release her, not a serious agreement. The חליצה still stands, but she cannot be forced to pay the two hundred זוז.

keyTerms.meaning: I am fooling you, meaning she was not serious

steps.whatToRemember: A mistaken חליצה that works for everyone is one done for a promised payment (two hundred זוז). In רב פפא's case, the woman does not have to pay, because she was only fooling the יבם.
steps.confusionAlert: Not paying does not cancel the חליצה. The חליצה is valid; רב פפא only says she does not owe the money.

phrases.english: He said to him: "I am fooling you"
phrases.notes: רב פפא is speaking to אביי, on behalf of his sister-in-law.

phrases.english: is what she did to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's instruction in step 14 that she must pay.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the duty to pay the money; the חליצה itself stays valid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The promise was never meant seriously, so it does not create a real obligation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two-hundred-זוז method frees the woman, and she is not forced to pay, because she was only fooling the יבם.

steps.title: The escaping prisoner and the ferryman
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a ברייתא: a man running from prison promised a ferryman a whole דינר for a ride, but he only has to pay the normal fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: A man was escaping from prison and came to a ferry. He told the ferryman, 'Take a דינר and bring me across.' The ferryman gets only his normal fee.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a source to back up what he said in step 15, that the woman does not have to pay the two hundred זוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prisoner was desperate, so he promised far more than the normal price. The ברייתא says he does not have to keep that promise and pays only the usual fee. This case looks a lot like the woman who promised the יבם money just to get her חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it taught? (a way of bringing a proof from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One who was running away from prison,
and there was a ferry in front of him,
and he said to him: Take a dinar and bring me across.
phrases.notes: A דינר is much more than a normal ferry ride costs.

phrases.english: He gets nothing more than his usual fee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's ruling in step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The woman does not have to pay the יבם the promised two hundred זוז.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an escaping prisoner who promised a ferryman too much and pays only the usual fee.

steps.title: The same reason applies to the woman
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we see that a person can say 'I was fooling you,' and the woman can say the same thing to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that he can say to him, 'I was fooling you.' Here too, she can say, 'I was fooling you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pulls the reason out of the ferry case and applies it to the woman's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prisoner pays only the normal fee because he can claim he never really meant his big promise. In the same way, the woman can claim she never really meant to pay the two hundred זוז, so she does not owe it.
steps.whatToRemember: A promise made under pressure, like the prisoner's or the woman's, can be undone by saying 'I was fooling you.'

phrases.english: So we see that he can say to him:
I was fooling you.
Here too, she can say: I was fooling you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אָמַר לֵיהּ מְשַׁטֶּה אֲנִי בָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pulls the reason out of the ברייתא in step 16 and applies it to the woman.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The woman can say she was fooling the יבם, so she does not have to pay the two hundred זוז.

steps.title: אביי asks about רב פפא's parents
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב פפא where his father and mother are. Both are in the city. אביי looks at them, and (in some versions) they die.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where is your father? He said: In the city. Where is your mother? He said: In the city. He set his eye on them, and they died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that happened right after this ruling, between אביי and רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text itself only gives the questions, the answers, and that אביי set his eye on the parents. It does not explain why. The words 'and they died' appear in round brackets.

keyTerms.meaning: he set his eye on them (an intense, harmful look)

phrases.english: He said to him: Where is your father?
phrases.notes: אביי is the one asking, and רב פפא is the one answering.

phrases.english: He said to him: In the city.
Where is your mother?
He said to him: In the city.
He set his eye on them (and they died).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, 'and they died.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A short story that follows the end of the discussion between אביי and רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story, not a ruling: אביי asks about רב פפא's parents and sets his eye on them.

steps.title: Mistaken and forced: חליצה compared to גט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a mistaken חליצה is valid but a mistaken גט is invalid, and a forced חליצה is invalid but a forced גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A mistaken חליצה is valid. A mistaken גט is invalid. A forced חליצה is invalid. A forced גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא that compares חליצה and גט in two situations: a mistake and force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules go in opposite directions. A mistake does not ruin a חליצה but does ruin a גט. Force ruins a חליצה but does not ruin a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: a גט the husband was forced to give

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the pairs. The rules flip: for a mistake, חליצה is valid and גט is not. For force, גט is valid and חליצה is not.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A mistaken חליצה is valid.
A mistaken bill of divorce is invalid.
A forced חליצה is invalid.
A forced bill of divorce is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about mistaken and forced חליצה and גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mistaken חליצה is valid and a mistaken גט is invalid. A forced חליצה is invalid and a forced גט is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the next discussion: why should force affect חליצה and גט differently?

steps.title: How can a forced גט be different from a forced חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. If the husband ends up saying 'I want to,' then a חליצה like that should also be valid. If he never says it, then a גט should also be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he said 'I want to,' then even a חליצה should also be valid. And if he did not say 'I want to,' then a גט should also not be valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's difference between a forced גט and a forced חליצה, and this question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא tries both possible cases. If the person is forced until he agrees and says 'I want to,' that should work for both חליצה and גט. If he never agrees, it should fail for both, so the ברייתא's difference seems hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the details?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he said, 'I want to,'
then even a חליצה should also be valid.
And if he did not say, 'I want to,'
then a bill of divorce should also not be valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דְּאָמַר רוֹצֶה אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ברייתא's difference between a forced חליצה and a forced גט from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a forced גט is valid but a forced חליצה is invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases treat חליצה and גט the same. Saying 'I want to' makes both valid, and not saying it makes both invalid, so there is no room for the difference.

steps.title: Forced cases depend on whether he says 'I want to'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that a mistake always gives the same result, but a forced חליצה or גט can go either way, depending on whether he says 'רוצה אני.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: a mistaken חליצה is always valid, and a mistaken גט is always invalid. A forced חליצה and a forced גט are sometimes valid and sometimes invalid. If he says 'I want to,' it works. If he does not say 'I want to,' it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20 by reading the ברייתא in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 asked: if the man says 'I want to,' a forced חליצה should be valid too, and if he does not, a forced גט should be invalid too. The answer rereads the ברייתא: a mistake always gives a fixed result (חליצה valid, גט invalid), but force does not. With force, both חליצה and גט follow the same rule: valid if he says 'רוצה אני,' invalid if he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: the גמרא rereads a statement
Done by mistake, when someone was tricked or misinformed
Forced, done under pressure from the court
'I want to': the words that show agreement

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as 'forced חליצה is always invalid, forced גט is always valid.' After this answer, both forced cases follow the same rule: it all depends on whether he says 'רוצה אני.'

phrases.english: This is what it means:
A mistaken חליצה is always valid,
and a mistaken גט is always invalid.
A forced חליצה and a forced גט:
sometimes valid and sometimes invalid.
This one is where he said 'I want to,'
that one is where he did not say 'I want to.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: mistake always gives a fixed result, while force depends on saying 'רוצה אני'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that forced חליצה is always invalid and forced גט is always valid
steps.terutzMaskana: A forced חליצה or גט is valid if he says 'רוצה אני' and invalid if he does not

steps.title: Proof from forcing a person to bring a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that forcing someone until he says 'רוצה אני' counts as his own will, both for קרבנות and for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'He shall offer it' teaches that we force him to bring it. Could it be totally against his will? The פסוק says 'by his will.' How can both be true? We force him until he says 'I want to.' The same is true with women's גיטין: we force him until he says 'I want to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the idea that 'I want to,' said under pressure, counts as real agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say two opposite things: the קרבן is forced, and it is 'by his will.' The ברייתא settles this: pressure that leads him to say 'I want to' makes it his will. The ברייתא says outright that גיטין work the same way, which supports the rule from Step 21.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for forcing a man to give a גט until he says 'רוצה אני,' which is how a בית דין can force a divorce and still have a valid גט.

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches:
'He shall offer it':
this teaches that we force him.
Could it be totally against his will?
The פסוק says: 'by his will.'
How can both be true?
We force him until he says 'I want to.'
And you find the same with women's גיטין:
we force him until he says 'I want to.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in Step 21
steps.raayaObject: Forcing someone until he says 'רוצה אני' counts as his free will
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 1:3 ('יקריב אותו לרצונו'), which applies the same rule to גיטין
steps.whatToRemember: A mistake gives a fixed result: חליצה valid, גט invalid. Under force, both work only if he says 'רוצה אני.'

steps.title: חליצה and מיאון may be done even without recognizing the people
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a court may do חליצה and מיאון even if it does not know who the people are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, who said in the name of רב הונא: We do חליצה even if we do not recognize the people, and we do מיאון even if we do not recognize them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: whether the court must know who is standing in front of it before doing חליצה or מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a court checks who people are before acting. Here רב הונא says the court does not need to know for sure that this man is really the יבם, or that this girl is really married to this husband. The court can still do the חליצה or the מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: We let a young girl do מיאון, refusing a marriage made while she was a minor
Recognize, know who the people are

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: רבא said that רב סחורה said that רב הונא said:

phrases.aramaic: חוֹלְצִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין,
phrases.english: We do חליצה even if we do not recognize them,

phrases.aramaic: מְמָאֲנִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין.
phrases.english: we do מיאון even if we do not recognize them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה and מיאון may be done even if the court does not recognize the people

steps.title: No document without recognizing the people
steps.stepSummary: Because the court does not check who the people are, it may not write a חליצה or מיאון document unless it recognizes them, so that a later court is not misled.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we do not write a חליצה document unless we recognize them, and we do not write a מיאון document unless we recognize them. This is because we worry that a later court will make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב הונא's teaching from Step 23 with a rule that follows from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חליצה or מיאון may have been done without checking who the people were, a written document could make it look as if their identity was confirmed. A later בית דין might trust the document and let the wrong woman remarry. So a document is written only when the people are recognized.

keyTerms.meaning: A document stating that חליצה took place
A document stating that a מיאון took place
A court that makes a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: Doing חליצה or מיאון does not require recognizing the people, but writing a document about it does.

phrases.english: Therefore we do not write a חליצה document
unless they recognize them,
and we do not write a מיאון document
unless they recognize them,
because we worry about a court making a mistake.
phrases.notes: This means a later court, which might see the document and think the people's identity was already checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A rule that follows from רב הונא's statement in Step 23
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Documents of חליצה or מיאון are written only if the court recognizes the people, so that a later court is not misled

steps.title: רבא's own view: the court must recognize the people first
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a court may not do חליצה or מיאון unless it recognizes the people involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא himself says: we do not do חליצה unless we recognize the people, and we do not do מיאון unless we recognize the people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives his own opinion, which is the opposite of what רב הונא said in the previous steps. He says the court must know who the people are before doing חליצה or מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the court can act without checking who the people are. רבא disagrees and puts the checking at the start: the court itself must make sure it knows who the man and woman are. This sets up his next point about the documents.

keyTerms.meaning: They recognize, they know who the people are
They perform מיאון, a young girl's refusal of a marriage arranged for her

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב הונא's view in step 23. רבא here says the opposite: the court must recognize the people before acting.

phrases.english: And Rava himself says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹלְצִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכִּירִין,
phrases.english: We do not perform חליצה unless they recognize the people,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְמָאֲנִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכִּירִין.
phrases.english: and we do not perform מיאון unless they recognize the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב הונא's ruling in steps 23–24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court may perform חליצה or מיאון only if it recognizes the people involved.

steps.title: So the documents may be written without recognizing the people
steps.stepSummary: Because the court already checked who the people are, a חליצה or מיאון document may be written even by someone who does not recognize them. We do not worry that the court made a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore we may write a חליצה document even if we do not recognize the people, and we may write a מיאון document even if we do not recognize them. We are not concerned that the court made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws the result of his rule. Since the court checked the people at the start, whoever writes the document afterward does not need to recognize them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 24. There, the court did not check, so the document could only be written by someone who knew the people. Here the court already checked, so the document can rely on the court, and we assume the court did its job properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A document confirming that חליצה took place
A document confirming that a מיאון took place
We are not concerned, we do not worry about
A court that makes a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the court acts without recognizing the people, so the document needs recognition. רבא: the court must recognize the people, so the document does not. Each puts the check at a different point.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the two views agree that a check is needed somewhere. They only disagree about whether it happens at the act itself or when the document is written.

phrases.english: Therefore we may write a חליצה document
even if they do not recognize the people,
and we may write a מיאון document
even if they do not recognize the people,
and we are not concerned about a mistaken court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of רבא's rule in step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under רבא, חליצה and מיאון documents may be written without recognizing the people, because the court already checked and we do not suspect it of error.
